skill.name: openspec-daem0n-bridge
skill.description: Connects OpenSpec workflows with Daem0n-MCP memory by importing specs, recalling prior decisions, and recording archived change outcomes.
skill.summary: Sync OpenSpec requirements, proposals, and archived outcomes with Daem0n memory.
skill.author: DasBluEyedDevil

security_audit.summary: Most static external command alerts are Markdown backtick false positives or MCP call examples. The real risks are narrow local shell reads of OpenSpec files and automatic persistence of project specification data into Daem0n memory.

remediation.issue: Automatic OpenSpec import can persist private requirements without explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before the first import, and show which files and memory categories will be written.

remediation.issue: Shell examples use placeholders for spec names and archive ids.
remediation.suggestion: Use structured file APIs where possible, or quote and validate path components before executing shell commands.

remediation.issue: Archived proposals and task files may contain sensitive implementation details.
remediation.suggestion: Ask the user before recording archive learnings, and allow redaction of confidential details.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Persistence of Project Specifications
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the agent to automatically import OpenSpec contents into Daem0n memory after detecting an openspec directory. This can persist confidential requirements and design context without a clear user approval step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The auto-import trigger and remember_batch workflows are explicit. The main uncertainty is whether the configured Daem0n-MCP memory stays local or leaves the workspace.

content.user_title: Sync OpenSpec Workflows With Daem0n Memory
content.value_statement: OpenSpec decisions can drift when prior requirements and outcomes are hard to find. This skill connects specs, proposals, and archived changes to Daem0n-MCP memory.
actual_capabilities: Detects an openspec/specs directory in the project workspace.
Imports OpenSpec spec summaries into Daem0n-MCP memory.
Extracts MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, and SHOULD NOT requirement language.
Recalls relevant memories before creating a new OpenSpec proposal.
Records proposal intent with OpenSpec tags and pending status.
Turns archived changes into learnings and links them to decisions.
limitations: Requires Daem0n-MCP memory tools to be available in the agent session.
Assumes the project uses the standard openspec directory layout.
Uses local shell examples for file discovery and file reads.
Does not validate OpenSpec content for correctness or completeness.

use_cases.title: Import Existing Specs
use_cases.description: Sync current OpenSpec requirements into memory before starting implementation work.

use_cases.title: Prepare Safer Proposals
use_cases.description: Review relevant specs, warnings, and past decisions before drafting a new proposal.

use_cases.title: Capture Archived Outcomes
use_cases.description: Convert completed OpenSpec changes into reusable learnings for future planning.
use_cases.target_user: Team member closing completed architecture work

prompt_templates.title: Import Specs
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for syncing current OpenSpec files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Sync the OpenSpec specs in this repository to Daem0n memory and summarize what was imported.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh Memory
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow after specs have changed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refresh the OpenSpec memory for this project and tell me which rules, warnings, and patterns changed.

prompt_templates.title: Check Proposal Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning before creating a proposal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Before I propose the [feature] change, recall relevant OpenSpec memories, rules, warnings, and past decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Record Archived Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow after implementation and archive.
prompt_templates.prompt: Record the outcome for archived OpenSpec change [change-id], create learnings, and link them to the original decision memory.

output_examples.output: The assistant reports imported specs, extracted rule counts, created memory categories, and any warnings found during parsing.
The assistant returns relevant specs, patterns to follow, warnings from past work, prior decisions, and rules to confirm.
The assistant summarizes the archived change, records whether it worked, creates learnings, and links them to the proposal decision.

best_practices: Review the import summary before relying on stored memories for planning.
Use clear OpenSpec change ids so proposal and archive records stay linked.
Redact confidential details before storing specs or archived outcomes in memory.
anti_patterns: Do not import private specifications into shared memory without approval.
Do not rely on stale memories after OpenSpec files have changed.
Do not treat remembered rules as a replacement for reading the current spec.

faq.question: What does this skill connect?
faq.answer: It connects OpenSpec specs and change workflows with Daem0n-MCP memory records.

faq.question: Does it create OpenSpec files?
faq.answer: No. It reads existing OpenSpec files and stores related context in memory.

faq.question: Can it help before writing a proposal?
faq.answer: Yes. It recalls related specs, warnings, rules, and past decisions for the feature.

faq.question: Does it require Daem0n-MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflows depend on Daem0n-MCP memory tools.

faq.question: What should I review before using it?
faq.answer: Review whether OpenSpec files contain confidential requirements before importing them into persistent memory.

faq.question: Can it record completed changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can turn archived OpenSpec changes into learnings and link them to earlier decisions.
